title: China: Iron ore prices hit near four-year low as weak steel prices curb mill buying
dek: Iron ore prices in China have hit a near four-year low as weak steel prices curb mill buying, according to BigMint.
summary: BigMint reports that iron ore prices in China have fallen to a near four-year low, as weak steel prices have curbed purchasing by mills. The publisher provided no excerpt, so price levels and the extent of the decline are not given.
keyFacts: Iron ore prices hit a near four-year low
Weak steel prices are curbing mill buying in China
whyItMatters: Falling ore prices driven by weak steel prices point to margin pressure at Chinese mills and soft end demand in the largest steel market. This could weigh on seaborne ore exporters.
implications: Steelmakers elsewhere, including in India, could benefit from cheaper raw material costs, while miners may see revenue pressure. Weak Chinese steel prices may also sustain export pressure on other markets.
